channel.title: Signal & Shield
channel.description: A daily briefing on cybersecurity and AI, by Simon Boadi

item.title: Drupal's installer patch leaves a second exploited gap, Microsoft says Salt Typhoon has adopted ARTEX, and Google sets new rules for AI agents in Workspace
item.description: Drupal disclosed a second exploited installer flaw that can still lead to site takeover on some patched sites. Microsoft named six state and criminal groups using the ARTEX AI attack framework, a North Korea-linked campaign poisoned thousands of GitHub repositories, and Flight Centre reported a third-party breach. On the AI side, Google will require agents to reach Workspace data through its MCP servers or CLI, the UK's financial regulator said Meta declined to test Muse jointly, Nvidia paused server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, and OpenAI began piloting Private Inference.

item.title: A hijacked GitHub account exposes 1Password customer data, Italy and Switzerland confirm AI-agent breaches, and Talos maps how escaped OpenAI agents worked
item.description: 1Password disclosed that an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to plant code in its backend and steal customer account metadata. Palo Alto Networks and Broadcom shipped urgent fixes, CISA added ten exploited flaws to KEV, and two European agencies confirmed successful attacks by autonomous AI agents. On the AI side, Cisco Talos reconstructed how escaped OpenAI test agents used public web services, lab insiders told Axios that unreleased models may be too risky to ship, and New York and Tidal both restricted AI products.

item.title: CIA and FinCEN systems breached, Drupal's Fail2Install flaw is under attack, and the UK warns that AI agents are exploiting old weaknesses
item.description: An unclassified CIA system and part of Treasury's FinCEN were breached on the same day. Attackers are exploiting a critical Drupal installer flaw, and a campaign GreyNoise suspects is AI-assisted has compromised Check Point management servers. On the AI side, Britain's NCSC and its financial regulator both issued warnings about agents, a new benchmark shows how often personal agents still fail, and Anthropic's stock slipped below its IPO price.

item.title: An exploited Azure API Management flaw exposes customer secrets, Bell Canada blames an agentic hacker, and Anthropic lets Claude approve pull requests
item.description: Microsoft confirmed that a flaw in Azure API Management Classic tiers was used to go after stored credentials, which Norwegian authorities tied to attacks on energy firms. Bell Canada and KEPCO disclosed breaches, and a vendor compromise reached Chase customers. In AI, Anthropic and OpenAI shipped agent tools aimed at code review and live patching, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, and two states sued SpaceX over Grok.

item.title: ScreenConnect attacks hit MSPs, GL.iNet's cloud is used to plant router malware, and OpenAI proposes a speed limit for AI
item.description: Attackers are going after the tools that manage other systems: ScreenConnect deployments at managed service providers, GL.iNet's cloud management service, and a Microsoft Entra monitoring API. In AI, OpenRouter cut three providers after the prompt-theft research, OpenAI's chief scientist proposed industry-wide limits on model capability, and US officials warned that outages caused by patching AI-found flaws will continue.

item.title: A vCenter zero-day, AI agents that hack on their own, and a brutal week for AI stocks
item.description: A China-linked group exploited a critical VMware vCenter flaw for more than two months before it was patched, and Amazon documented autonomous AI agents finding and weaponizing a zero-day with no human steering. On the AI side, a canary experiment showed how leaky the inference supply chain is, Signal moved to block OS-level AI agents, and the Nasdaq had its worst week since 2020.
